source_text: Si anima peccaverit et mentietur proximo in deposito vel societate, delictum est. Fides inter fratres altare est. Mendacium spoliat communionem.
thought_title: Sin against a neighbor and the altar of faith
orientation: Origen is explaining the spiritual meaning of Leviticus 4:1, applying the law of sin against a neighbor to the moral life of believers.
pass_a_gloss: If [the] soul [shall] have sinned and [shall] have lied to [the] neighbor in [a] deposit or [a] partnership, [it] is [a] sin. Faith between brothers [is] [an] altar. [A] lie despoils [the] communion.

choices.why: The source uses delictum, not peccatum, so a distinct rendering preserves the legal-moral nuance of a fault against a neighbor.
The future tense in a conditional clause is rendered as a present habitual action in English, matching the generalizing force of the Latin.
Societas denotes a shared undertaking or business relationship, not a general social bond.
Spoliat has a forceful sense of despoiling or robbing, which fits the image of lying destroying the communion built on faith.

bible_refs.note: Si anima peccaverit et mentietur proximo in deposito vel societate

pass_b_english: If a soul sins and lies to a neighbor about a deposit or a partnership, it is a transgression (Leviticus 5:21 (6:2)). Faith between brothers is an altar. Lying strips away communion.

problems.why: This citation format may not match LXX numbering; Leviticus 6:2 in Hebrew is 5:21 in LXX
problems.ruling: Leviticus 6:2 (Hebrew/MT) = Leviticus 5:21 in LXX; early Christian Latin texts often follow LXX numbering, potentially misleading readers.

fixed: The citation was updated to reflect LXX numbering with the Hebrew in parentheses, per the brief's instruction to use standard English book names and modern numbering with a note where LXX numbering differs.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'it is a fault/trespass,' not 'transgression.' 'Delictum' is a specific term for a fault requiring reparation, distinct from 'peccatum' (sin).
last_rejected.ruling: 'Delictum' can mean transgression; rendering within normal range. No meaning lost or changed.
